title: This Fox Hunts by Listening to Insects Chew Underground
subject: bat-eared fox

scenes.text: This fox finds its dinner by listening to the ground.
It stands about a foot tall, but its ears grow up to five inches long.
At night it walks slowly, nose low, ears pointed forward, like a satellite dish.
It can hear termites chewing grass, and larvae chewing their way out of buried dung beetle balls.
Then it digs straight to the spot.
One fox can eat about one million termites a year, all found by sound.

description:
The bat-eared fox finds insects by listening for them underground.
Its ears grow up to five inches long, and one fox can eat about 1.15 million termites a year.
Could you find anything by listening to the ground?
thumbnail_text: THE FOX THAT LISTENS TO DIRT
